ax.f: (now nonstandard or dialectal, especially African-American Vernacular, MLE and Bermuda) Alternative form of ask.

s.g: A tool for felling trees or chopping wood etc. consisting of a heavy head flattened to a blade on one side, and a handle attached to it.
An ancient weapon consisting of a head that has one or two blades and a long handle.
(informal, with the) A dismissal or rejection.
s.x: His girlfriend/boss/schoolmaster gave him the axe.

s.g: (figurative) A drastic reduction or cutback.
(slang, music) A gigging musician's particular instrument, especially a guitar in rock music or a saxophone in jazz.
(transitive) To fell or chop with an axe.
(transitive, figurative) To lay off, terminate or drastically reduce, especially in a rough or ruthless manner; to cancel.
s.x: The government announced its plans to axe public spending.

s.g: (archaic) The axle of a wheel.
To furnish with an axle.

axe.f: (now obsolete outside dialects, especially African-American Vernacular) Alternative form of ask.

axed.f: simple past and past participle of ax (all etymologies and senses)

s.g: Having a specified number of type of axis.
(figure skating) A jump that includes one (or more than one) complete turn and a half turn while in the air.
(intransitive, figure skating) To perform a jump of this kind.

axels.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of axel

s.g: (also figurative) A man who wields an axe.
(informal, music) A musician who plays a guitar or saxophone.
(biology, of a culture, sample, specimen, etc) Containing only a single species of microorganism.
s.x: This species has resisted all attempts at axenic culture.

s.g: (biology, of an organism) Isolated from organisms of any other species.

axes.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of ax and axe (all etymologies and senses)

s.g: Relating to, resembling, or situated on an axis
(anatomy) Belonging to the axis of the body, or to the axis of any appendage or organ
(botany) In the same direction as the axis, parallel to the axis.
s.x: The secondary xylem usually consists of axial and radial elements.

s.g: (physical chemistry, organic chemistry) Oriented parallel to the axis running through the centre of a cyclohexane ring, as opposed to equatorial. See Axial bond.
(ornithology) A flight feather that appears between the primaries and secondaries on some birds.
(dentistry) A plane parallel to the surface of a tooth.
In relation to, or in a line with, an axis; in the axial (magnetic) line.
(botany) The angle or point of divergence between the upper side of a branch, leaf, or petiole, and the stem or branch from which it springs.
The armpit, or the cavity beneath the junction of the arm and shoulder.
(entomology) The area that is located posterior to the transscutal articulation and anterior to the scutoscutellar suture.
Any of the feathers connecting the undersurface of the wing and the body, and concealed by the closed wing.
Of or pertaining to the axilla or armpit.
(botany) Situated in, or rising from, an axil; relating to an axil.
(medicine) A fatty and varnish-like substance produced in Mexico by an insect, Llaveia axin, used in the arts and locally in medicine, being regarded as a good vulnerary and resolvent.

axing.f: present participle and gerund of ax

s.g: An assault carried out with an axe.
(figurative) The process of something being axed or terminated.
Of or relating to value theory, the philosophical field of axiology.
Of or relating to values themselves.
(uncountable, philosophy) The study of value(s), as regards origin, nature, functions, types, and interrelations; value theory.
(countable) The particular value-theory of a philosopher, school of thought, etc.
s.x: In his axiology, G. E. Moore maintains that "good" is the name of a simple, indefinable quality.

s.g: (philosophy) A seemingly self-evident or necessary truth which is based on assumption; a principle or proposition which cannot actually be proved or disproved.

(logic, mathematics, proof theory) A fundamental assumption that serves as a basis for deduction of theorems; a postulate (sometimes distinguished from postulates as being universally applicable, whereas postulates are particular to a certain science or context).
An established principle in some artistic practice or science that is universally received.
s.x: The axioms of political economy cannot be considered absolute truths.

s.g: Self-evident or unquestionable. [from 18th c.]
(mathematics) Relating to or containing axioms. [from 19th c.]
By the use of axioms; in the form of an axiom.
The reduction of some system or concept to a set of axioms.
The result of establishing a concept within a system of axioms; axiomatic system.
(physics) A hypothetical subatomic particle postulated to resolve certain symmetry problems concerning the strong nuclear force.
(geometry) An imaginary line around which an object spins (an axis of rotation) or is symmetrically arranged (an axis of symmetry).
s.x: The Earth rotates once a day on its axis

s.g: (mathematics) A fixed one-dimensional figure, such as a line or arc, with an origin and orientation and such that its points are in one-to-one correspondence with a set of numbers; an axis forms part of the basis of a space or is used to position and locate data in a graph (a coordinate axis)
(anatomy) The second cervical vertebra of the spine
(anatomy) An imaginary, visualized plane separating two morphologically similar parts of an organism
(psychiatry) A form of classification and descriptions of mental disorders or disabilities used in manuals such as the DSM (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders)
A deer native to Asia, of species Axis axis.
Exhibiting symmetry around an axis; exhibiting cylindrical symmetry; axially symmetric
A small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
(obsolete) Shoulder.
The pin or spindle on which a wheel revolves, or which revolves with a wheel.
A transverse bar or shaft connecting the opposite wheels of a car or carriage; an axletree.
(geometry, astronomy, archaic) An axis.
Synonym of axletree.
A carpet made in Axminster imitating the Turkey carpet, noted for its thick and soft pile.
A critically endangered salamander found in the elevated lakes of Mexico, Ambystoma mexicanum.
s.x: She is going on a tour to see axolotls at Mexico.

s.g: (cytology) A nerve fibre which is a long slender projection of a nerve cell, and which conducts nerve impulses away from the body of the cell to a synapse.
(cytology) Of or pertaining to an axon.
(biology) A bundle of nine microtubules forming the internal scaffolding of a cilium, with two extra central microtubules connecting the others if the cilium is motile
(technical drawing) Describing a projection in which the horizontal and vertical axes are to the same scale, but the third axis is reduced to allow for perspective.
(historical) A native or inhabitant of Axum or a descendant of such a person.
(historical) Of or relating to Axum or the Axumites.
